findings.issue_text: Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members: the server now applies limit/offset with a default limit of 50 to all groups (previously only automatic groups were capped at 200), and no pagination UI was added to the public members template, so groups with more than 50 members show only the first 50 with no indication that more exist

Pagination off-by-one: totalPages = Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 is one too high when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, and because showingLast/next/findMembers clamps allow offset == user_count, the admin can navigate to an empty 'last' page (e.g., '3/3' or '2/2' showing an empty member list); clamps should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) / cap offset at (totalPages-1)*limit, and the same flaw leaves the admin on an empty page after member removals when offset lands on the new user_count

The new <form class="form-horizontal"> wrapper in the admin group template has no submit-event handler: pressing Enter in the group-name text field or user-selector triggers a native form submission to the current URL, causing a full page reload that discards all unsaved edits

findMembers builds the members URL from the two-way-bound, live-edited name field ('/groups/' + this.get('name') + '/members.json'), so after an unsaved rename every pagination click and post-add/remove reload requests members for a non-existent group name, causing 404s and stale member lists that invite duplicate retries; the fetch should key off the immutable id or saved name

No in-flight guard or cancellation on findMembers: each response overwrites offset, user_count, and members, so rapid next/previous clicks or a pagination click racing an add/remove reload can resolve out of order, letting an earlier-issued response land last and silently revert the view to a previous page or transiently omit a just-added user

Public group members page only fetches one page (default limit: 50, offset: 0) and the public members template has no pagination controls, so groups with more than 50 members silently show only the first 50 members with no indication anything is missing — a regression since all members were previously listed (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:6-10, app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6)

The client-supplied `limit` parameter on the public groups#members endpoint is uncapped (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb), allowing unauthenticated requests like `?limit=99999999` to load and serialize the entire membership of large groups (e.g., automatic trust_level_0) in a single request, enabling resource exhaustion

Public API response shape broken on GET /groups/:id/members (groups_controller.rb:22-37): response changed from a bare JSON array of GroupUserSerializer objects to a wrapped {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}} object, and results are now silently capped at 50 records by default (previously non-automatic groups returned the full list, automatic up to 200), breaking external API clients, plugins, and theme JS with no versioning, compat flag, or deprecation path

Public group members page silently truncated to 50 members (group-members.js.es6:12-16, members.hbs:6): the route now fires model.findMembers() with default limit 50 and the template iterates members, but no pagination controls or page state were added (unlike the admin page), so any public group with >50 members shows only the first 50 with no indication or way to see the rest

Admin::GroupsController#update silently sets visible = false whenever the param is absent (~line 36): group.visible = params[:visible] == 'true' is unconditional, so partial API updates (e.g. sending only alias_level) — including every old-format caller sending group: {...} since the nested params[:group] payload is now ignored — silently flip the group to hidden and return success_json, causing silent data corruption

PUT /admin/groups/:id now reads top-level name/alias_level/visible and ignores nested params[:group], so old-format callers get a 200 while their intended changes are silently dropped (and visible gets clobbered)
PATCH /admin/groups/:id still routes to update (Rails default) but the changes[add]/changes[delete] incremental-membership API is gone, so those callers now silently no-op

POST /admin/groups no longer accepts group[name]/group[usernames], so old clients fail with a blank-name 422 and membership can no longer be set at create time; none of these admin groups API contract changes include a deprecation, versioning, or compat shim

totalPages off-by-one in admin-group.js.es6 (~line 13): Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 should be Math.ceil, so when user_count % limit == 0 (e.g. exactly 100 members at limit 50) totalPages is 3, showingLast is false on page 2, and 'next' advances to an empty page 3/3; same defect surfaces after removing a member when the page lands exactly on a multiple

Group.findMembers() no longer always returns a promise (group.js ~line 13): the empty-name early return changed from Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) to a bare return (undefined), so plugin/theme code chaining .then() throws a TypeError in the 'new group' path, and the unannounced signature change also removed saveWithUsernames/createWithUsernames from the model surface

Admin::GroupsController#add_members 500s on array input (~line 57): params.require(:usernames).split(',') crashes with NoMethodError when a caller posts usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b (Rails array param), a stricter, undocumented input contract on a new externally reachable endpoint (the old incremental API tolerated arrays)

remove_member spec exercises an unroutable verb (admin/groups_controller_spec.rb ~line 91): it uses xhr :put, :remove_member but routes.rb:49 only declares delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member'; in production a PUT to that URL routes to add_members, and the spec passes only because rspec controller specs bypass routing, masking the verb contract

Add-members flow can silently fail on repeat (admin-group.js.es6 ~line 63): after addMembers succeeds the input isn't cleared, so clicking Add again re-submits the same usernames, the duplicate GroupUser fails validation, the 422 rejection is unhandled, and the member list never reloads with no user feedback

GET /admin/groups/:group_id/users route removed from config/routes.rb (~line 49): it appears to have been dead (no users action exists in Admin::GroupsController before or after this PR, so it 404'd anyway), but since it was a registered, externally reachable admin API URL, a one-time grep of plugins/external scripts should be done before shipping

Route/param mismatch: the new member routes (delete 'members' => groups#remove_member, put 'members' => groups#add_members) nested inside the admin resources :groups block supply the group id as params[:id], but add_members/remove_member in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb call params.require(:group_id), raising ActionController::ParameterMissing and returning 400 on every UI add/remove request — potentially making the PR's headline feature dead end-to-end (unless the routes are declared with param: :group_id)

add_members (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:65-82) returns success_json even when nothing was added: usernames.split(',') has no per-entry strip, unknown usernames (spaces after commas, typos, or group names picked from the selector autocomplete) are silently skipped by User.find_by_username, re-adding an already-present username is unguarded, and the frontend shows no error and doesn't clear the input — the admin gets zero signal the add failed; the endpoint should strip entries and report unmatched usernames in the response (or return 422)
No transaction wraps the per-iteration group.add(user) loop in add_members, so a mid-loop failure leaves partially-applied membership state

Off-by-one in totalPages (admin-group.js.es6:11-14): Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields one page too many when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 50 members with limit 50 shows '1/2'), letting next() navigate to a phantom empty page; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

No rejection handlers on any of the new member promise chains — findMembers, removeMember, and addMembers in discourse/models/group.js have no .catch, and admin_group_route.js / group-members.js.es6 call model.findMembers() fire-and-forget, so 400/403/422/500 failures are fully silent (e.g., a Guardian.ensure_can_see! 403 for hidden groups now silently renders an empty list instead of surfacing via route error handling as the old afterModel code did), leaving removed members on screen with no message or retry and stale user_count/members

The public members endpoint (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:24-25) accepts raw, unbounded limit/offset: ?limit=10000000 forces an unbounded query and serialization on a user-facing endpoint (memory/DoS vector), and negative values pass straight into limit()/offset() raising a SQL error → a trivially triggerable 500; values need clamping (cap at a few hundred, floor at 0)

remove_member raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound → 500 on stale/invalid input (member already removed elsewhere, stale UI list, or params[:user_id].to_i == 0 from junk input) because group.users.delete(user_id) looks up the association record; deletion should be idempotent — rescue or check membership and still return success

alias_level is silently dropped on group creation: the frontend's asJSON() sends alias_level, but the backend create action only assigns name/visible, so the alias level chosen on the 'new group' form is lost (saved as default 0) and must be re-entered with a second save

No in-flight guard on findMembers — rapid pagination clicks or an add/remove-triggered reload racing a pagination fetch produce concurrent overlapping requests whose responses apply setProperties in arrival order, so a slow older response can clobber a newer one and the displayed members won't match the displayed page/offset; no request token or isFetching flag exists

findMembers contract regression (group.js:19): returning undefined for empty-name groups (if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return; }) replaces the old Ember.RSVP.resolve([]), so any caller chaining .then gets a TypeError for new/unnamed groups — currently latent but a trap on a model used by two routes

No request-level/routing spec exists for the new add_members/remove_member endpoints — every spec in spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb is a controller spec that bypasses routing by passing group_id explicitly, so a route/param mismatch would pass CI; adding one routing-level spec would close the biggest reliability gap in the change

Off-by-one pagination bug in admin-group.js.es6: `totalPages = Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces a phantom last page when `user_count % limit == 0` — with the default limit of 50, a group with exactly 50 members shows totalPages: 2, and clicking 'next' sets offset to 50, returning an empty member list to the admin.
The new admin group pagination logic (currentPage, totalPages, next, previous) has zero unit tests, which would have caught the exact-multiple-of-limit edge case.

Breaking response-format change to GroupsController#members has no spec coverage: the payload changed from a flat serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}, the default limit dropped from 200 to 50, and pagination now applies to all groups (previously only automatic groups), yet no spec pins the new shape, meta values, ordering, or offset-beyond-count behavior, and any pre-existing spec asserting the old array format was not updated.

Public group members page now truncates to 50 members with no way to page: the public route fires a single findMembers() (limit 50, offset 0) and no pagination controls or offset-changing actions were added outside the admin controller, so groups with more than 50 members silently show only 50 members — an untested regression.
One new test exercises an unreachable request shape, testing a request that cannot actually occur in practice.

Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination controls: the backend hard-caps every members listing at limit 50 for all groups, while next/previous pagination actions were added only to the admin controller, so the public group-members route and template have no way to page past 50 members (groups_controller.rb:24-28, group-members.js.es6:10-13, members.hbs:6)

Pagination math is off-by-one, producing a blank phantom page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 instead of Math.ceil(user_count / limit), and both the next action and findMembers clamp offset to Math.min(offset + limit, user_count), permitting the invalid state offset == user_count; the correct max offset is (totalPages - 1) * limit (admin-group.js.es6:13, :33, group.js:21)

Pagination/view state (limit, offset, user_count, fetched members) and the side-effecting findMembers loader are embedded in the persistence model Discourse.Group, coupling the admin and public members UIs through one shared pagination implementation; the page-size default of 50 is duplicated client-side (limit: 50) and server-side (params[:limit] || 50) and will drift, and reads go through the public name-keyed endpoint while writes go through the admin id-keyed endpoint (group.js:8-10, :18-35)

The offset-boundary invariant (keep offset within [0, user_count]) is duplicated with divergent formulas in three places across two layers: the controller clamps offset + limit while the model clamps raw offset, so the layers disagree about which operations are legal and a fix in one place won't propagate (admin-group.js.es6:33, :44, group.js:21)

findMembers contract regression: the early-exit path for empty-name groups returns undefined instead of a promise (previously Ember.RSVP.resolve([])), making the return type 'Promise | undefined' so any future caller chaining .then()/.catch() will fail silently on new groups (group.js:19)

Breaking API contract changes shipped with no compatibility consideration: the members response changed from a bare array to a {members, meta} envelope and admin create/update params changed from nested group[...] to flat params, so external consumers (plugins, admin-API clients) break silently, and an old-style PUT /admin/groups/:id now finds the params nil and silently resets visible to false while ignoring the intended change (groups_controller.rb:30-33, admin/groups_controller.rb:22-40)

add_members/remove_member report success/failure decoupled from the actual mutation: group.add(user) and group.users.delete(user_id) persist join records immediately, but group.save and render_json_error only run afterwards, so an error response can describe state that was already mutated, and the non-transactional loop over usernames leaves the group half-updated while reporting success (admin/groups_controller.rb:65-97)

Unknown usernames are silently dropped in add_members — User.find_by_username skips typos/nonexistent users with no feedback while the endpoint renders success — compounded by the shipped client TODO that leaves the add-members input uncleared, so admins have no signal which names took effect and may re-submit the same string (admin/groups_controller.rb:71-75, admin-group.js.es6 addMembers)

Unbounded limit on the public members endpoint: (params[:limit] || 50).to_i has no maximum clamp, so any client can request /groups/:name/members?limit=1000000 and the new meta contract echoes it back; the old hole existed only for automatic groups but this PR extends the parameter to every group (groups_controller.rb:24)

The new admin group template renders raw {{user_count}} instead of using the existing userCountDisplay presentation logic (whose documented purpose is to hide the ugly zero), so empty groups display (0) and 0/0 pagination, and the same datum now has two divergent display paths that will drift (admin/templates/group.hbs:14 vs group.js:12-16)

Inconsistent group-name normalization between create and update: create strips whitespace via (params[:name] || '').strip but update assigns group.name = params[:name] with no strip, so the same input ' bob ' is accepted on create but rejected or stored dirty on update; normalization belongs in one place such as the model (admin/groups_controller.rb:24 vs :40)

admin-group.js.es6: totalPages = Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 is off-by-one when user_count % limit == 0 (100 members, limit 50 yields totalPages 3 when only 2 pages exist), so showingLast fails on the real last page and 'next' stays enabled; correct math is Math.ceil(user_count/limit) (or floor((user_count-1)/limit)+1).

models/group.js findMembers clamps offset with Math.min(user_count, ...), which permits offset == user_count so the server legitimately returns zero rows — the clamp should pin to the last page start, not user_count. This produces a phantom empty '3/3' page when clicking next past the end, and strands the UI on an empty '2/2' page after removing the last member of a page (51 members dropping to 50 leaves offset 50), making it appear members were lost.

admin/groups_controller.rb create only assigns name and visible, silently discarding the alias_level sent by the rewritten asJSON(): new groups persist with alias_level 0 while the form keeps displaying the admin's selection, so the save appears green while the real value was dropped, and the divergence persists until a second save. The new .create spec suite covers only name-stripping and asserts nothing about alias_level, hiding this silent pass.

usernames is singleton Ember controller state that is never reset — setupController only sets the model and addMembers deliberately doesn't clear the input — so text typed while editing group A remains when navigating to group B, and clicking 'Add' then adds those users to the wrong group (membership grants permissions); after a successful add, the retained text also invites a duplicate re-submission. Regression from the old code that derived usernames from members per model.

groups_controller.rb add_members is a silent no-op for unknown usernames: the User.find_by_username guard skips non-matching names with no error, no report, and success_json, so a typo'd username (also whitespace-padded names, since split(',') isn't trimmed) 'succeeds' while nothing happened, leaving the admin zero feedback as the UI reloads an unchanged list.

add_members is neither idempotent nor atomic: there is no membership-existence check before group.add(user) — re-adding an existing member either raises on the group_users uniqueness constraint (a 500 to the admin) or inserts duplicate join rows — and there is no transaction around the loop, so a mid-list failure leaves earlier usernames already persisted with no rollback, a partial-failure state the admin can't reason about.
The public GET /groups/:name/members response changes from a bare serialized array to {members, meta}, silently breaking every existing consumer of that endpoint (plugins, scripts, mobile clients).

Admin update unconditionally assigns group.visible = params[:visible] == 'true' with no .present? guard (unlike alias_level), and admin create/update now require flat top-level params instead of group: {...}, so any legacy admin-API caller using the old payload shape that doesn't send top-level visible silently flips the group to invisible while getting a 200 back.

The new pagination protocol — the meta: {total, limit, offset} contract plus client-side clamping — has zero spec coverage: there are no controller specs for groups#members at all (meta values, offset beyond count, limit echo), and the removed .update membership specs were not replaced with pagination/add-remove edge cases (removing the last member of a page, adding beyond the current page).

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members: the server now applies limit/offset with a default limit of 50 to all groups (previously only automatic groups were capped at 200), and no pagination UI was added to the public members template, so groups with more than 50 members show only the first 50 with no indication that more exist

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes member listing to always apply `limit`/`offset` with a default `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` for *all* groups, whereas previously limiting/pagination was only applied for `group.automatic?` (and defaulted to 200). On the client side, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now requests `/groups/<name>/members.json` with `limit`/`offset` and stores results in `members`, but the public template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` simply iterates `{{#each m in members}}` and no pagination controls were added there. Therefore groups with >50 members will show only the first page with no UI indicating more members exist or allowing navigation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination off-by-one: totalPages = Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 is one too high when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, and because showingLast/next/findMembers clamps allow offset == user_count, the admin can navigate to an empty 'last' page (e.g., '3/3' or '2/2' showing an empty member list); clamps should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) / cap offset at (totalPages-1)*limit, and the same flaw leaves the admin on an empty page after member removals when offset lands on the new user_count

The new <form class="form-horizontal"> wrapper in the admin group template has no submit-event handler: pressing Enter in the group-name text field or user-selector triggers a native form submission to the current URL, causing a full page reload that discards all unsaved edits

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a literal HTML `<form class="form-horizontal">` wrapper in `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs` but does not attach any Ember `{{action ... on="submit"}}` handler (nor any `onsubmit`/`{{view}}` wrapper) to prevent native submission. The template contains text inputs (`{{text-field ...}}`, `{{user-selector ...}}`) and `<button>` elements without explicit `type` attributes; in HTML, `<button>` defaults to `type="submit"`. With no submit handler, pressing Enter in an input (or default submit behavior) can trigger a real form submit to the current URL, causing a full page reload and losing unsaved state. This behavior is directly implied by the added `<form>` and lack of submit interception in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers builds the members URL from the two-way-bound, live-edited name field ('/groups/' + this.get('name') + '/members.json'), so after an unsaved rename every pagination click and post-add/remove reload requests members for a non-existent group name, causing 404s and stale member lists that invite duplicate retries; the fetch should key off the immutable id or saved name

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group#findMembers` the request URL is built from `this.get('name')` (`/groups/` + name + `/members.json`). In the admin UI, non-automatic groups render a live-editable `text-field value=name` while still showing the member list and pagination/actions (`next`/`previous` call `group.findMembers()`, and `addMembers`/`removeMember` reload via `self.findMembers()`). After an unsaved rename, these reloads/pagination will fetch members for the new (nonexistent) name, which `GroupsController#members` resolves strictly by name (`find_group` uses `lower(name) = ?`), leading to 404s/stale lists. The diff shows no guarding to use the saved name or id for member fetches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No in-flight guard or cancellation on findMembers: each response overwrites offset, user_count, and members, so rapid next/previous clicks or a pagination click racing an add/remove reload can resolve out of order, letting an earlier-issued response land last and silently revert the view to a previous page or transiently omit a just-added user

Public group members page only fetches one page (default limit: 50, offset: 0) and the public members template has no pagination controls, so groups with more than 50 members silently show only the first 50 members with no indication anything is missing — a regression since all members were previously listed (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:6-10, app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the public `GroupsController#members` endpoint to always paginate (`limit` default 50, `offset` default 0) for all groups, returning `{members, meta}` instead of the full list (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb). On the client, `group-members` now calls `model.findMembers()` without supplying any paging UI (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6), and the public template simply iterates `{{#each m in members}}` with no pagination controls (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs). Previously, non-automatic groups were not limited (only automatic groups applied limit/offset), so this can regress behavior by showing only the first 50 members with no way/indication to view the rest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The client-supplied `limit` parameter on the public groups#members endpoint is uncapped (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb), allowing unauthenticated requests like `?limit=99999999` to load and serialize the entire membership of large groups (e.g., automatic trust_level_0) in a single request, enabling resource exhaustion

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit)` with no upper bound. This allows a client to request an arbitrarily large `limit` (e.g. `?limit=99999999`) and force the server to load and serialize a very large members list in one response (`serialize_data(members, GroupUserSerializer)`), which is a resource-exhaustion/DoS risk. The change also applies this pagination logic to all groups (not just automatic ones as before), widening exposure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public API response shape broken on GET /groups/:id/members (groups_controller.rb:22-37): response changed from a bare JSON array of GroupUserSerializer objects to a wrapped {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}} object, and results are now silently capped at 50 records by default (previously non-automatic groups returned the full list, automatic up to 200), breaking external API clients, plugins, and theme JS with no versioning, compat flag, or deprecation path

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare array, with no limit for non-automatic groups and default 200 only for automatic groups) to a wrapped JSON object `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` and applies a default `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` to all groups (`limit/offset` always used). This is a substantial, potentially breaking contract change for any callers expecting the old shape/full list, but it appears intentional to support pagination (the JS `findMembers()` and templates/routes were updated accordingly), so it's best treated as a compatibility/upgrade concern rather than an outright correctness defect proven within this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page silently truncated to 50 members (group-members.js.es6:12-16, members.hbs:6): the route now fires model.findMembers() with default limit 50 and the template iterates members, but no pagination controls or page state were added (unlike the admin page), so any public group with >50 members shows only the first 50 with no indication or way to see the rest

adjudication.rationale: In the public group members route, `setupController` now sets `model` to the group and calls `model.findMembers()` without any pagination UI/state (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6). `Group#findMembers` always requests `/groups/:name/members.json` with `limit`/`offset` (defaults `limit: 50, offset: 0` in the model), and the backend `GroupsController#members` now always applies `limit` (default 50) and `offset` for all groups, not just automatic ones. The public template was changed to iterate `{{#each m in members}}` (members.hbs), which will therefore show only the first page (50) with no controls/indication to reach remaining members. This is a concrete behavior regression visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::GroupsController#update silently sets visible = false whenever the param is absent (~line 36): group.visible = params[:visible] == 'true' is unconditional, so partial API updates (e.g. sending only alias_level) — including every old-format caller sending group: {...} since the nested params[:group] payload is now ignored — silently flip the group to hidden and return success_json, causing silent data corruption

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` is executed unconditionally. If the `visible` param is omitted, `params[:visible]` is nil and the expression evaluates to false, causing the group to be hidden on any partial update that doesn’t include `visible`. Additionally, the controller no longer reads the old nested `params[:group]` payload (previously `payload = params[:group]`), so legacy callers sending only `group: { ... }` would omit top-level `visible` and trigger this silent flip while still returning `success_json`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PUT /admin/groups/:id now reads top-level name/alias_level/visible and ignores nested params[:group], so old-format callers get a 200 while their intended changes are silently dropped (and visible gets clobbered)

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update, the code now reads params[:alias_level], params[:visible], and params[:name] at the top level and no longer looks at params[:group] (old update_put used payload = params[:group]). This means old-format requests sending {group: {...}} will have their changes ignored. Additionally, visible is unconditionally set via `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`, so if a caller omits top-level visible (e.g., only sends params[:group][:visible]), it will be clobbered to false while the request can still return success_json (200), causing silent unintended changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PATCH /admin/groups/:id still routes to update (Rails default) but the changes[add]/changes[delete] incremental-membership API is gone, so those callers now silently no-op

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the PATCH-specific incremental membership handling (`update_patch` and the `request.patch?` branch) from `Admin::GroupsController#update`, but `resources :groups` in `config/routes.rb` will still generate the default PATCH `/admin/groups/:id` route. The new `update` method ignores `params[:changes]` entirely and will just `save` without applying add/delete membership changes, returning success JSON if nothing else fails—so PATCH callers using the old `changes[add]/changes[delete]` contract will silently have no effect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: POST /admin/groups no longer accepts group[name]/group[usernames], so old clients fail with a blank-name 422 and membership can no longer be set at create time; none of these admin groups API contract changes include a deprecation, versioning, or compat shim

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the admin groups create/update payload shape from nested `params[:group][:name]` / `params[:group][:usernames]` to top-level `params[:name]` etc. (`Admin::GroupsController#create` now does `group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip` and no longer reads usernames; `#update` now reads `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`). As a result, an older client POSTing `{ group: { name: "bob", usernames: "..." } }` would yield `params[:name] == nil` => blank name and likely a validation failure/422, and there is no longer any way to set membership at create time via that endpoint. The diff shows no compat shim or dual-parameter support.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages off-by-one in admin-group.js.es6 (~line 13): Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 should be Math.ceil, so when user_count % limit == 0 (e.g. exactly 100 members at limit 50) totalPages is 3, showingLast is false on page 2, and 'next' advances to an empty page 3/3; same defect surfaces after removing a member when the page lands exactly on a multiple

Group.findMembers() no longer always returns a promise (group.js ~line 13): the empty-name early return changed from Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) to a bare return (undefined), so plugin/theme code chaining .then() throws a TypeError in the 'new group' path, and the unannounced signature change also removed saveWithUsernames/createWithUsernames from the model surface

Admin::GroupsController#add_members 500s on array input (~line 57): params.require(:usernames).split(',') crashes with NoMethodError when a caller posts usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b (Rails array param), a stricter, undocumented input contract on a new externally reachable endpoint (the old incremental API tolerated arrays)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff introduces `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` followed by `usernames.split(",")`. If a caller submits a Rails array param (e.g., `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), `params[:usernames]` will be an `Array`, which does not respond to `split`, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500. The new admin route `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` makes this endpoint callable, and the controller code does not normalize/validate the type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member spec exercises an unroutable verb (admin/groups_controller_spec.rb ~line 91): it uses xhr :put, :remove_member but routes.rb:49 only declares delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member'; in production a PUT to that URL routes to add_members, and the spec passes only because rspec controller specs bypass routing, masking the verb contract
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both point out that the remove_member spec uses xhr :put while the route for groups#remove_member is defined with DELETE, meaning the test is using the wrong HTTP verb and may bypass routing expectations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Add-members flow can silently fail on repeat (admin-group.js.es6 ~line 63): after addMembers succeeds the input isn't cleared, so clicking Add again re-submits the same usernames, the duplicate GroupUser fails validation, the 422 rejection is unhandled, and the member list never reloads with no user feedback

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `actions.addMembers` has a TODO noting the input should be cleared but it currently reuses `this.get("usernames")` on every click and does not reset it after success. Also, it does not handle errors from `model.addMembers(...)` (no `.catch` / feedback), and `Group.addMembers` in `group.js` only refreshes the member list inside `.then(...)`, so any server-side failure would result in no reload and no UI feedback. However, the specific claim that duplicates *will* cause a 422 validation failure is not directly verifiable from this diff alone (server behavior for duplicate adds isn’t shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: GET /admin/groups/:group_id/users route removed from config/routes.rb (~line 49): it appears to have been dead (no users action exists in Admin::GroupsController before or after this PR, so it 404'd anyway), but since it was a registered, externally reachable admin API URL, a one-time grep of plugins/external scripts should be done before shipping

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `config/routes.rb` removing `get "users"` under the admin groups resource and replacing it with `delete "members"` and `put "members"`. In `Admin::GroupsController` (both before/after in this diff), there is no `users` action defined, so the route likely pointed to a non-existent controller action. The finding’s suggestion to grep plugins/external scripts is a compatibility/release concern tied directly to this externally reachable URL change, not a code defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Route/param mismatch: the new member routes (delete 'members' => groups#remove_member, put 'members' => groups#add_members) nested inside the admin resources :groups block supply the group id as params[:id], but add_members/remove_member in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb call params.require(:group_id), raising ActionController::ParameterMissing and returning 400 on every UI add/remove request — potentially making the PR's headline feature dead end-to-end (unless the routes are declared with param: :group_id)
matched_golden_ids: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the routes provide the group identifier as params[:id], but the controller actions expect/read params[:group_id] (even requiring it), causing requests to fail and breaking group membership add/remove functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:65-82) returns success_json even when nothing was added: usernames.split(',') has no per-entry strip, unknown usernames (spaces after commas, typos, or group names picked from the selector autocomplete) are silently skipped by User.find_by_username, re-adding an already-present username is unguarded, and the frontend shows no error and doesn't clear the input — the admin gets zero signal the add failed; the endpoint should strip entries and report unmatched usernames in the response (or return 422)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username| ... User.find_by_username(username) ... end` without trimming each entry. This means inputs like `"bob, alice"` will look up `" alice"` (leading space) and fail to add that user, yet the action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds. The silent skipping of unknown/whitespace-polluted usernames and unconditional success response can result in members not being added with no signal to the admin, which is a correctness/behavior defect exposed by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No transaction wraps the per-iteration group.add(user) loop in add_members, so a mid-loop failure leaves partially-applied membership state

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",").each` and calls `group.add(user)` for each found user, then calls `group.save` once at the end. There is no explicit `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction` around the loop, so if `group.add(user)` (or the later `group.save`) can fail/raise after some additions, earlier membership changes could already be applied while later ones are not. The diff doesn’t show what `Group#add` does (whether it persists immediately or is purely in-memory), so this is a robustness/atomicity concern grounded in the new loop but not fully verifiable as a definite defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one in totalPages (admin-group.js.es6:11-14): Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields one page too many when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 50 members with limit 50 shows '1/2'), letting next() navigate to a phantom empty page; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)
matched_golden_ids: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same off-by-one pagination bug: using Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 overcounts pages when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, causing a phantom empty page. It even suggests the correct fix (Math.ceil).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No rejection handlers on any of the new member promise chains — findMembers, removeMember, and addMembers in discourse/models/group.js have no .catch, and admin_group_route.js / group-members.js.es6 call model.findMembers() fire-and-forget, so 400/403/422/500 failures are fully silent (e.g., a Guardian.ensure_can_see! 403 for hidden groups now silently renders an empty list instead of surfacing via route error handling as the old afterModel code did), leaving removed members on screen with no message or retry and stale user_count/members

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new async flows do not propagate or handle failures: `Discourse.Group#findMembers`, `#removeMember`, and `#addMembers` in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js` all return `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` with no rejection handling. More importantly, both `admin_group_route.js` and `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now call `model.findMembers();` in `setupController` without returning/awaiting the promise (fire-and-forget), whereas the old `afterModel` returned the promise chain. From the diff alone, an AJAX 4xx/5xx will no longer block the route transition or be surfaced via route error handling, and the UI can remain stale/empty with no feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The public members endpoint (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:24-25) accepts raw, unbounded limit/offset: ?limit=10000000 forces an unbounded query and serialization on a user-facing endpoint (memory/DoS vector), and negative values pass straight into limit()/offset() raising a SQL error → a trivially triggerable 500; values need clamping (cap at a few hundred, floor at 0)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff changes pagination to `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then directly applies them to `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no clamping/validation. This allows arbitrarily large limits (e.g. `?limit=10000000`) causing a potentially huge query + serialization on a public endpoint, and permits negative values which can trigger DB/ActiveRecord errors (500). The finding is directly supported by the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound → 500 on stale/invalid input (member already removed elsewhere, stale UI list, or params[:user_id].to_i == 0 from junk input) because group.users.delete(user_id) looks up the association record; deletion should be idempotent — rescue or check membership and still return success

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, `user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i` can become `0` (junk input) or refer to a deleted user. The subsequent `group.users.delete(user_id)` on an AR association commonly resolves non-model arguments by doing a `User.find(user_id)`, which raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` for invalid IDs and would bubble to a 500 since there’s no rescue/guard. The method is intended to be a simple membership removal endpoint, so it should be idempotent/robust against stale/invalid user_ids.

adjudication_records.issue_text: alias_level is silently dropped on group creation: the frontend's asJSON() sends alias_level, but the backend create action only assigns name/visible, so the alias level chosen on the 'new group' form is lost (saved as default 0) and must be re-entered with a second save

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: frontend `Discourse.Group#asJSON()` includes `alias_level` (and `create()` POSTs `data: this.asJSON()`), so the new-group form can send an alias level. However, backend `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `name` and `visible` (no `alias_level`), so the chosen alias level is ignored on creation and will default (likely 0) until a subsequent update (`#update` does handle `alias_level`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No in-flight guard on findMembers — rapid pagination clicks or an add/remove-triggered reload racing a pagination fetch produce concurrent overlapping requests whose responses apply setProperties in arrival order, so a slow older response can clobber a newer one and the displayed members won't match the displayed page/offset; no request token or isFetching flag exists
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe a race condition caused by findMembers() being asynchronous without proper handling/guarding: the controller can apply results out of order or before data is available, leading to stale/incorrect member data being shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers contract regression (group.js:19): returning undefined for empty-name groups (if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return; }) replaces the old Ember.RSVP.resolve([]), so any caller chaining .then gets a TypeError for new/unnamed groups — currently latent but a trap on a model used by two routes
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the function has a code path (early return / missing explicit return) that results in returning undefined instead of a value/promise, which can break callers expecting a returned value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No request-level/routing spec exists for the new add_members/remove_member endpoints — every spec in spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb is a controller spec that bypasses routing by passing group_id explicitly, so a route/param mismatch would pass CI; adding one routing-level spec would close the biggest reliability gap in the change

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new admin routes for group membership changes (`put "members" => "groups#add_members"`, `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` in `config/routes.rb`) and new controller actions that require `params[:group_id]` (`Admin::GroupsController#add_members` / `#remove_member`). The accompanying tests in `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` invoke the controller actions directly via `xhr` and pass `group_id` explicitly, which does not validate that routing actually supplies the expected param key/path. There is no request/routing spec in the diff to catch a potential route-to-param mismatch, so adding one would improve reliability without implying a current functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one pagination bug in admin-group.js.es6: `totalPages = Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces a phantom last page when `user_count % limit == 0` — with the default limit of 50, a group with exactly 50 members shows totalPages: 2, and clicking 'next' sets offset to 50, returning an empty member list to the admin.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which yields an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 50/50 => 2). The `next` action then sets `offset` to `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, so from 0 it becomes 50, and `Group#findMembers` requests `offset=50`. The server (`GroupsController#members`) applies `.limit(limit).offset(offset)`, so `offset=50` with `total=50` returns an empty `members` list. This matches the described phantom last page behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new admin group pagination logic (currentPage, totalPages, next, previous) has zero unit tests, which would have caught the exact-multiple-of-limit edge case.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial client-side pagination logic in `admin-group.js.es6` (`currentPage`, `totalPages`, and `next`/`previous` actions), but the only tests added/modified are Ruby controller specs (`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`) and none cover this JS pagination behavior. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap: e.g., `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which has an exact-multiple-of-limit edge case that JS tests could catch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking response-format change to GroupsController#members has no spec coverage: the payload changed from a flat serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}, the default limit dropped from 200 to 50, and pagination now applies to all groups (previously only automatic groups), yet no spec pins the new shape, meta values, ordering, or offset-beyond-count behavior, and any pre-existing spec asserting the old array format was not updated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a flat array response) to a JSON object `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`, and also introduces a universal `limit`/`offset` (default `limit` now `(params[:limit] || 50).to_i`) rather than only applying pagination to automatic groups. In the provided spec changes, only `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` is modified/added; there is no spec in this diff that exercises `GroupsController#members` to pin the new response shape, meta fields, ordering, or pagination semantics. The claim about an existing spec asserting the old array format cannot be verified from this diff, but the lack of new/updated spec coverage for the changed endpoint is grounded and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page now truncates to 50 members with no way to page: the public route fires a single findMembers() (limit 50, offset 0) and no pagination controls or offset-changing actions were added outside the admin controller, so groups with more than 50 members silently show only 50 members — an untested regression.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply pagination (`limit` default 50, `offset` default 0) for *all* groups and returns `{members, meta}` instead of the full serialized array. On the client, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now requests with `limit`/`offset` and sets `members` on the group model, but the public `group-members` route/template adds no pagination controls or actions to change `offset` (unlike the admin controller which adds `next/previous`). `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` iterates `members`, so the public members page will only show the first page (50) with no way to reach the rest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: One new test exercises an unreachable request shape, testing a request that cannot actually occur in practice.

adjudication.rationale: The new controller spec for `.remove_member` includes `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the diff’s routing exposes `remove_member` only via `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members` (`routes.rb`: `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`). A PUT request to that path cannot occur in practice, so this test exercises an unreachable request/verb shape rather than the real route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination controls: the backend hard-caps every members listing at limit 50 for all groups, while next/previous pagination actions were added only to the admin controller, so the public group-members route and template have no way to page past 50 members (groups_controller.rb:24-28, group-members.js.es6:10-13, members.hbs:6)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply a `limit` defaulting to 50 and an `offset` for *all* groups (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`, `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`), whereas previously only automatic groups were limited. On the client side, admin UI adds next/previous pagination controls/actions, but the public `group-members` route/template does not add any pagination controls or offset/limit handling; it just calls `model.findMembers()` once and the public template iterates `{{#each m in members}}` with no navigation. As a result, public group members listings will show only the first page (50) with no way to access the rest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination math is off-by-one, producing a blank phantom page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 instead of Math.ceil(user_count / limit), and both the next action and findMembers clamp offset to Math.min(offset + limit, user_count), permitting the invalid state offset == user_count; the correct max offset is (totalPages - 1) * limit (admin-group.js.es6:13, :33, group.js:21)

Pagination/view state (limit, offset, user_count, fetched members) and the side-effecting findMembers loader are embedded in the persistence model Discourse.Group, coupling the admin and public members UIs through one shared pagination implementation; the page-size default of 50 is duplicated client-side (limit: 50) and server-side (params[:limit] || 50) and will drift, and reads go through the public name-keyed endpoint while writes go through the admin id-keyed endpoint (group.js:8-10, :18-35)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does embed pagination/view state on the persistence model: `Discourse.Group` now has `limit: 50`, `offset: 0`, `user_count: 0` and `findMembers()` both performs the fetch and mutates model properties including `members` (`setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members: ... })`). Both admin and public member UIs call `model.findMembers()` in their routes (`admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6`), so they share this single pagination implementation. The default page size is indeed duplicated client-side (`limit: 50` in `group.js`) and server-side (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` in `GroupsController#members`), which could drift later. Also, the read uses the public name-keyed endpoint (`/groups/` + `name` + `/members.json`) while membership writes use admin id-keyed endpoints (`/admin/groups/:id/members.json` via `addMembers`/`removeMember`). These are concrete, diff-grounded coupling/architecture concerns rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The offset-boundary invariant (keep offset within [0, user_count]) is duplicated with divergent formulas in three places across two layers: the controller clamps offset + limit while the model clamps raw offset, so the layers disagree about which operations are legal and a fix in one place won't propagate (admin-group.js.es6:33, :44, group.js:21)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does duplicate offset clamping/pagination boundary logic across layers: the admin controller computes offsets in `next`/`previous` (Math.min/Math.max against `user_count`/0) and also derives `currentPage`/`totalPages` from `offset/limit` (admin-group.js.es6), while the model independently clamps `offset` inside `findMembers` (group.js). These are separate formulas/locations for keeping offset in range and computing paging, so future fixes/changes would need to be made in multiple places. However, the finding’s claim that the layers currently “disagree” about legality isn’t clearly borne out by the diff—both effectively clamp into [0, user_count], just in different spots.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers contract regression: the early-exit path for empty-name groups returns undefined instead of a promise (previously Ember.RSVP.resolve([])), making the return type 'Promise | undefined' so any future caller chaining .then()/.catch() will fail silently on new groups (group.js:19)

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.findMembers` the empty-name early exit changed from `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` to a bare `return;`, so it now returns `undefined` on that path while returning an Ajax promise otherwise (`group.js`: `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }`). That is a real contract/inconsistency regression, but within this diff all updated callers (`admin_group_route` / `group-members` route / controller actions) call `findMembers()` without chaining `.then()`, so the diff does not show an immediate runtime failure—it's primarily an API/edge-case hazard for any code expecting a promise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking API contract changes shipped with no compatibility consideration: the members response changed from a bare array to a {members, meta} envelope and admin create/update params changed from nested group[...] to flat params, so external consumers (plugins, admin-API clients) break silently, and an old-style PUT /admin/groups/:id now finds the params nil and silently resets visible to false while ignoring the intended change (groups_controller.rb:30-33, admin/groups_controller.rb:22-40)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce backward-incompatible request/response contract changes without any fallback: `GroupsController#members` switches from `render_serialized(members.to_a, ...)` (bare array) to an explicit `{ members: ..., meta: ... }` JSON envelope, while `Admin::GroupsController#create`/`update` switch from nested `params[:group]` payloads to flat params (`params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:alias_level]`). In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` is applied unconditionally, so a caller still sending the old nested payload (or omitting `visible`) will now silently set `visible` to `false` rather than preserving the existing value (or erroring), which is broken behavior / potential data-loss for existing clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members/remove_member report success/failure decoupled from the actual mutation: group.add(user) and group.users.delete(user_id) persist join records immediately, but group.save and render_json_error only run afterwards, so an error response can describe state that was already mutated, and the non-transactional loop over usernames leaves the group half-updated while reporting success (admin/groups_controller.rb:65-97)

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members and #remove_member, the mutation happens via `group.add(user)` and `group.users.delete(user_id)` before the subsequent `if group.save ... else render_json_error(group)` check. In Rails, these association operations typically persist join-table changes immediately, so `group.save` is not providing atomicity or rollback; an error path (if `group.save` were to fail) would not reflect the already-applied membership changes, and there’s no transaction around the multi-username loop. However, the diff doesn’t show a concrete way `group.save` would realistically fail here (the group is already persisted and no validated attributes are changed), so this is more of a correctness/architecture concern than a clearly triggered defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unknown usernames are silently dropped in add_members — User.find_by_username skips typos/nonexistent users with no feedback while the endpoint renders success — compounded by the shipped client TODO that leaves the add-members input uncleared, so admins have no signal which names took effect and may re-submit the same string (admin/groups_controller.rb:71-75, admin-group.js.es6 addMembers)

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the loop `usernames.split(",").each` only adds when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user and otherwise does nothing, yet the action still renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds—so typos/nonexistent usernames are silently ignored with no feedback. On the client side, `admin-group.js.es6` `addMembers` includes `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not clear `this.get("usernames")`, which can compound admin confusion/resubmission. This is a concrete UX/edge-case concern introduced by the new add-members flow, but not a strictly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded limit on the public members endpoint: (params[:limit] || 50).to_i has no maximum clamp, so any client can request /groups/:name/members?limit=1000000 and the new meta contract echoes it back; the old hole existed only for automatic groups but this PR extends the parameter to every group (groups_controller.rb:24)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and applies it directly to `group.users...limit(limit)` with no maximum clamp, and also returns it in `meta` (diff shows `limit: limit`). Because this endpoint is under `GroupsController` (public-facing) and the PR now applies `limit/offset` logic for all groups (previously only for `group.automatic?`), a client can request an arbitrarily large `limit` (e.g. `1000000`), causing potentially heavy queries/large responses. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/security defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new admin group template renders raw {{user_count}} instead of using the existing userCountDisplay presentation logic (whose documented purpose is to hide the ugly zero), so empty groups display (0) and 0/0 pagination, and the same datum now has two divergent display paths that will drift (admin/templates/group.hbs:14 vs group.js:12-16)

adjudication.rationale: In the new admin template, the member count is rendered as `({{user_count}})` (admin/templates/group.hbs within the `{{#if id}}` block). The Group model still defines `userCountDisplay` specifically to suppress showing `0` (“don't display zero its ugly”), but this presentation helper is not used here. Additionally, the template always renders `{{currentPage}}/{{totalPages}}`, and the controller computes both as `0` when `user_count == 0`, producing a visible `0/0` pagination display for empty groups. This is a concrete UI regression introduced by the diff and creates two divergent display paths for the same datum (`user_count` vs `userCountDisplay`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent group-name normalization between create and update: create strips whitespace via (params[:name] || '').strip but update assigns group.name = params[:name] with no strip, so the same input ' bob ' is accepted on create but rejected or stored dirty on update; normalization belongs in one place such as the model (admin/groups_controller.rb:24 vs :40)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Admin::GroupsController#create normalizes the group name with `(params[:name] || '').strip`, but Admin::GroupsController#update assigns `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic` without stripping. This can persist leading/trailing whitespace on update (or behave differently than create for the same input), resulting in inconsistent stored data and potentially broken lookups/routing that assume normalized names.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin-group.js.es6: totalPages = Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 is off-by-one when user_count % limit == 0 (100 members, limit 50 yields totalPages 3 when only 2 pages exist), so showingLast fails on the real last page and 'next' stays enabled; correct math is Math.ceil(user_count/limit) (or floor((user_count-1)/limit)+1).

adjudication.rationale: In admin-group.js.es6, totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 when user_count > 0. This overcounts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100/50 => 3 instead of 2). Because showingLast is based on currentPage == totalPages, the UI will not consider page 2 the last page, leaving "next" enabled. The next action can then advance offset to user_count (via Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)), and Group.findMembers will request offset=user_count, yielding an empty members page (offset 100, limit 50). This is a real behavioral defect visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: models/group.js findMembers clamps offset with Math.min(user_count, ...), which permits offset == user_count so the server legitimately returns zero rows — the clamp should pin to the last page start, not user_count. This produces a phantom empty '3/3' page when clicking next past the end, and strands the UI on an empty '2/2' page after removing the last member of a page (51 members dropping to 50 leaves offset 50), making it appear members were lost.
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same pagination bug: clamping the next offset to user_count allows offset == total, which returns an empty result set and creates a confusing/phantom last page (e.g., showing 2/2 or 3/3 with no members). The candidate adds extra scenarios but matches the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb create only assigns name and visible, silently discarding the alias_level sent by the rewritten asJSON(): new groups persist with alias_level 0 while the form keeps displaying the admin's selection, so the save appears green while the real value was dropped, and the divergence persists until a second save. The new .create spec suite covers only name-stripping and asserts nothing about alias_level, hiding this silent pass.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: client now posts `alias_level` on create (`Group.asJSON()` returns `{ name, alias_level, visible }` and `Group.create()` POSTs it), and the create UI still renders the alias level combo-box for new groups (`admin/templates/group.hbs` renders `combo-box ... value=alias_level` outside the `{{#if id}}` block). But `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `name` and `visible` and never reads `params[:alias_level]`, so the chosen alias level is silently dropped and the group persists with default `alias_level` (0) until a later `update` call. The new create spec only checks name stripping and does not assert alias_level, so it would not catch this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: usernames is singleton Ember controller state that is never reset — setupController only sets the model and addMembers deliberately doesn't clear the input — so text typed while editing group A remains when navigating to group B, and clicking 'Add' then adds those users to the wrong group (membership grants permissions); after a successful add, the retained text also invites a duplicate re-submission. Regression from the old code that derived usernames from members per model.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `admin-group` controller, `usernames` is just a plain property (`usernames: null`) and is only ever read/written via the user-selector binding and `addMembers`. `setupController` in `admin_group_route.js` no longer sets/reset `usernames` (it only does `controller.set("model", model); model.findMembers();`). Since Ember controllers are typically reused across route transitions, any previously entered `usernames` text can persist when switching between groups. The template always binds `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}`, and `addMembers` explicitly does not clear it (`// TODO: should clear the input`), so stale input can be submitted again and potentially applied to a different group’s model via `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb add_members is a silent no-op for unknown usernames: the User.find_by_username guard skips non-matching names with no error, no report, and success_json, so a typo'd username (also whitespace-padded names, since split(',') isn't trimmed) 'succeeds' while nothing happened, leaving the admin zero feedback as the UI reloads an unchanged list.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the diff shows `usernames.split(",").each` and `User.find_by_username(username)` with no `strip`/normalization and no else-path for unknown users; it then renders `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. This means typo’d or whitespace-padded usernames will be ignored and the request still reports success, resulting in a silent no-op as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members is neither idempotent nor atomic: there is no membership-existence check before group.add(user) — re-adding an existing member either raises on the group_users uniqueness constraint (a 500 to the admin) or inserts duplicate join rows — and there is no transaction around the loop, so a mid-list failure leaves earlier usernames already persisted with no rollback, a partial-failure state the admin can't reason about.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the diff shows `usernames.split(",").each` calling `group.add(user)` for each found user, with no explicit membership-existence check and no surrounding transaction (only a final `group.save`). This means the operation is not designed to be atomic (a failure/exception mid-loop would not be rolled back by any transaction shown in the diff) and is not explicitly idempotent. However, the claim that re-adding an existing member will definitely 500 or create duplicates depends on the (not-shown) implementation of `Group#add` / association constraints, so the concrete failure mode cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The public GET /groups/:name/members response changes from a bare serialized array to {members, meta}, silently breaking every existing consumer of that endpoint (plugins, scripts, mobile clients).

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the response changes from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }` (an object with `members` and `meta`). This is a backwards-incompatible change to the public `GET /groups/:name/members` endpoint and will break any existing consumers expecting an array, unless they are updated in lockstep.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin update unconditionally assigns group.visible = params[:visible] == 'true' with no .present? guard (unlike alias_level), and admin create/update now require flat top-level params instead of group: {...}, so any legacy admin-API caller using the old payload shape that doesn't send top-level visible silently flips the group to invisible while getting a 200 back.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update, the diff changes from nested params[:group] to flat top-level params and sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` without a presence check. If a legacy client continues sending `group: { visible: ... }` (or omits top-level `visible`), `params[:visible]` will be nil and the expression evaluates false, flipping the group to invisible while still returning 200 on successful save. This behavior is directly shown in the new `update` method (`group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`) and the removal of the old `payload = params[:group]` structure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new pagination protocol — the meta: {total, limit, offset} contract plus client-side clamping — has zero spec coverage: there are no controller specs for groups#members at all (meta values, offset beyond count, limit echo), and the removed .update membership specs were not replaced with pagination/add-remove edge cases (removing the last member of a page, adding beyond the current page).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new pagination response contract in `GroupsController#members` (returns `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`) and client-side pagination/clamping logic in `Discourse.Group#findMembers` (uses `result.meta.*` and clamps `offset`). However, the only updated specs are for `Admin::GroupsController` (`.add_members`, `.remove_member`, etc.); there are no specs added/modified for `GroupsController#members` to assert the new JSON shape or meta values. Also, while old incremental membership-update specs were removed, the replacements cover add/remove endpoints but not pagination edge cases like last-page removal or offset/limit behavior. This is a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap rather than an immediate functional defect.
